headline: the risk premium has come out of the front of the curve - the best entry in a month, but nothing underneath it has changed
commentary: UK power spot is 142.51 £/MWh and the gas front month has fallen to 176.89 p/therm, down 10.2% in four sessions and the lowest since late August. The cause is a risk premium unwinding rather than more gas arriving: Saudi Arabia is reported to be bringing its damaged East-West pipeline back on line this week, a possible US-Iran meeting at the UN and US pressure on Ukraine over strikes on Russian refineries have taken the edge off near-term supply fears, and the weather pattern into next week is being read as bearish for winter demand. None of that adds a molecule to European storage, which is still near 68% of capacity, so we would treat this as a window rather than a turn - a fall built on risk coming out is one a cold snap can put back. Where it fell matters as much as how far. For the third reading running the move is concentrated in the front of the curve: Winter 26 is down 11.1% since Friday, Winter 27 only 3.9% and Winter 28 1.2%. So a 12-month contract starting this October is around 1.06 p/kWh cheaper on a wholesale-equivalent basis than it was on Friday, a 24-month only 0.64 p/kWh. Longer term still wins, by less than it did last week. On the volatility a fixed price removes: day-ahead power touched minus £1.89 last Saturday against a peak hour of 178.37 £/MWh on Tuesday evening.

gas.note: NBP front-month (Oct 26) is 176.89 p/therm, down 10.2% since 18 September, and next winter has come down with it - Winter 26 175.54, Dec 26 181.56, Jan 27 180.54. The curve still steps down hard beyond it: Winter 26 175.54, Winter 27 124.00 (-29.4%), Winter 28 88.40 (-28.7%), or -49.6% across the two years, with Summer 27 at 126.25. That shape is still the case for term - a 24-month contract blends next winter down with cheaper 2027 and 2028, and a 36-month reaches the third step. But note the Winter 26 to Winter 27 discount has NARROWED for the second edition running, 38.3% on 14 Sep to 34.7% on 18 Sep to 29.4% today, because the prompt is giving back an outage and geopolitical premium the far curve never carried. Third confirmation of the rule: near-term risk prices into the front, and so does its relief. Winter 27 has now held between 123.75 and 130.25 across five readings, which is why the term argument is anchored on it, and Winter 28 at 88.40 confirms last week's 89.50 first appearance.
